cases.expected: Discriminator registered in context with empty mapping; no exception thrown.
cases.description: When the schema does not contain a "discriminator" property, the method should skip all conditional logic and simply register the provided discriminator.

group: Discriminator present but no existing context entry

cases.expected: Discriminator registered in context; no exception thrown.
cases.description: Even though the schema defines a discriminator, because the context does not already have a discriminator for the schema location, the method should bypass the merging logic and just register the discriminator.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException with message containing "attempts redefining the discriminator property"
cases.description: When a nested schema tries to redefine the discriminator's propertyName, the method must throw a JsonSchemaException.

group: Add mapping when root has no mapping

cases.expected: Root discriminator now contains mapping { "dog": { "$ref": "#/definitions/Dog" } }; no exception thrown.
cases.description: If the root discriminator lacks a "mapping" field but the nested schema provides one, the method should copy the entire mapping object to the root discriminator.

cases.expected: Root mapping now contains both "cat" and "dog" entries; the existing "cat" entry is unchanged because the node reference is identical; no exception thrown.
cases.description: When both root and child discriminators have mappings, the method should merge new keys and ignore keys that already exist with the same JsonNode instance.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException with message containing "discriminator mapping redefinition from cat"
cases.description: If a child schema attempts to map a key that already exists in the root discriminator but points to a different JsonNode, the method must throw a JsonSchemaException.

group: Both mappings null – no merge performed

cases.expected: Root discriminator unchanged (still no mapping); no exception thrown.
cases.description: When both the root discriminator and the child discriminator lack a "mapping" field, the method should simply register the discriminator without attempting any merge.

group: Schema without discriminator but context already has one – registration overwrites

cases.expected: The discriminator stored in the context for "/root" becomes the empty object passed in (i.e., previous mapping is overwritten). No exception is thrown.
cases.description: When the schema does not contain a "discriminator" property but the context already holds a discriminator for the same schema location, the method should skip merging logic and simply register the supplied discriminator, effectively replacing the previous entry.

group: Child mapping null – root mapping unchanged

cases.expected: Root discriminator mapping remains exactly { "cat": { "$ref": "#/definitions/Cat" } }. No exception is thrown.
cases.description: The child schema defines a discriminator object without a "mapping" field. Since the root already has a mapping, the method should perform no merge and leave the root mapping untouched.

group: Child mapping empty object – no merge performed

cases.expected: Root discriminator mapping stays unchanged (contains only "cat"). No exception is thrown.
cases.description: The child discriminator provides an empty "mapping" object. The merge loop iterates over zero fields, so the existing root mapping should remain unchanged.

group: Mapping key redefinition with equal content but different JsonNode instances throws

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException with message containing "discriminator mapping redefinition from cat" is thrown.
cases.description: Both root and child discriminators map the same key "cat" to JSON objects that are structurally identical but are distinct JsonNode instances. Because the implementation compares node references (using !=), this situation is treated as a conflict and must raise an exception.
When the supplied discriminator argument is null, the method attempts to call discriminator.get("mapping") and throws a NullPointerException before any registration.

group: Discriminator mapping non-object node throws ClassCastException

cases.description: The discriminator argument contains a "mapping" field that is a JSON string (or any non‑ObjectNode). The method casts it to ObjectNode, causing a ClassCastException.

group: Schema discriminator mapping non-object node throws ClassCastException

cases.description: The schema's discriminator contains a "mapping" field that is a JSON string (or any non‑ObjectNode). When the method casts it to ObjectNode, a ClassCastException is thrown.
